title: Optimization of Sparse Sensor Layouts and Data-Driven Reconstruction Methods for Steady-State and Transient Thermal Field Inverse Problems
content: This paper addresses the inverse problem of temperature fields in both steady-state and transient heat conduction scenarios. A comprehensive approach is proposed, integrating the optimization of sparse sensor layouts with a data-driven reconstruction methodology, aiming to enhance the accuracy and computational efficiency of temperature field reconstruction. Initially, models incorporating various irregular heat source distributions and differing boundary conditions for steady-state and transient heat conduction are constructed, with numerical solutions obtained through the finite difference method. Following this, the study systematically investigates the impact of various sensor layout optimization strategies on reconstruction accuracy, including random point selection, S-OPT method, correlation coefficient filtering method (CCFM), and uniform point selection. Additionally, diverse sampling methods such as Latin hypercube sampling, Sobol sequence sampling, and maximum-minimum distance sampling are employed to establish a multifaceted database construction scheme. Experimental results demonstrate the robustness of the Gappy Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) and Gappy C-POD methods across different modal conditions, particularly exhibiting strong stability when the number of modes is low (1-5 modes). The Gappy C-POD method, when paired with CCFM point selection and maximum distance sampling, effectively mitigates reconstruction deviations. Conversely, while the POD-MLP and POD-RBF methods maintain high overall accuracy at greater modal numbers (>10 modes), they display significant sensitivity to sensor placement and database size. Based on the findings of this study, the Gappy C-POD method is recommended as a mainstream approach for tackling the inverse problem of temperature fields, particularly when coupled with well-considered sensor layout optimization strategies to enhance both the accuracy and efficiency of field reconstruction. This research provides a novel perspective on solving heat conduction inverse problems, particularly highlighting the theoretical importance of integrating data-driven methods with sensor layout optimization.
